items.title: GTA 6’s Best Song Is A Nelly Furtado Cover From Azerbaijan
items.description:
One of the mainstay features in Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto series is radio
stations that can be listened to while driving in cars or, as in GTA 6, on the
go if you acquire headphones. As a music-discovery vehicle, GTA: Vice City
introduced me to many '80s classics across a variety of genres. With GTA 6
taking players to Leonida, in which Vice City is located, it's apt that the game
features music that many probably would never hear anywhere else. One of the
radio stations you'll find in the game is Kaleidoscope FM. It features covers of
very-well-known songs that are performed by artists from around the world. It's
a fantastic hook for a radio station and delivers some of the catchiest and
most-unexpected covers from artists that have a pretty low profile outside of
their home countries. The first song I heard on the station, and the one that
remains my absolute favorite, is a cover of Nelly Furtado's "Say It Right" from
Azerbaijani artists Alim Qasimov and Farghana Qasimova. The duo are known for
performing Mugham, a type of music that blends poetry, melody, and
improvisation. I had never heard of them before playing GTA 6, but the music
instantly transported me to my youth listening to Qawwali, a type of music that
is rooted in Islamic sufism.  Initially, my exposure to Qawwali, a type of music
that is over 600 years old, was limited to my own home, but it has since gained
a worldwide following thanks to Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, who is known as the King
of Kings of Qawwali. These days it's pretty common to hear songs that either
sample or are inspired by Qawwali, but, even so, hearing Mugham in GTA 6 was a
huge surprise. I didn't expect to be playing Rockstar's latest opus and be
reminded of Qawwali.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?is=GsirJ2mQmdOdZt1a&v=6iA9fogYpLA I already love
"Say It Right"--I think it's one of Furtado and producers Timbaland and Danja's
best--but this cover draws out the melancholic soul that underpins the original,
giving it a more emotional weight. Much of that can be attributed to the
religious mysticism that both Mugham and Qawwali evoke.  What I appreciate about
this cover is how brilliantly it allows the unfamiliar to grasp what makes
Mugham and Qawwali so beautiful by presenting it through a song that many people
already have some familiarity with. Both types of music are performed by an
ensemble, but the improvisational nature means that others are encouraged to
contribute. The use of the kamancheh, tar, and daf, along with the vocals
covering Furtado's chorus and the khananda's additions, come together to make
the cover feel magical.  There are other songs that will no doubt catch you by
surprise on Kaleidoscope FM--another favourite is a South Asian cover of
"Careless Whisper." Naturally, I was intrigued by how this station came to be
and, according to Ivan Pavlovich, Rockstar's vice president of music, it stems
from an obsession that studio co-founder Sam Houser has. “Historically, we have
always loved to champion a quirky, concept-driven station," Pavlovich told
GameSpot. "Sam loves foreign-language covers of his favorite songs and thought
this could be that station for GTA VI. Tracking down rights holders proved
particularly tricky in certain countries." The biggest surprise, however, is the
radio station's host: Academy Award winner Jeremy Irons. "Jeremy Irons has the
perfect voice as the travel-weathered host telling tall tales of his adventures
from around the world," Pavlovich added. "Jeremy loved the script, and nailed
the wry humor of his character in one session. Hopefully, this station makes
fans smile as much as we did when we were making it." Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews
are available now. GameSpot gave it a 10/10, saying that it sets the standard
for open worlds impossibly high.

“Historically, we have always loved to champion a quirky, concept-driven
station," Pavlovich told GameSpot. "Sam loves foreign-language covers of his
favorite songs and thought this could be that station for GTA VI. Tracking down
rights holders proved particularly tricky in certain countries."

The biggest surprise, however, is the radio station's host: Academy Award winner
Jeremy Irons.

"Jeremy Irons has the perfect voice as the travel-weathered host telling tall
tales of his adventures from around the world," Pavlovich added. "Jeremy loved
the script, and nailed the wry humor of his character in one session. Hopefully,
this station makes fans smile as much as we did when we were making it."

Grand Theft Auto 6 reviews are available now. GameSpot
[https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/grand-theft-auto-6-review/] gave it a 10/10,
saying that it sets the standard for open worlds impossibly high.

items.title: PSN Went Down Sorta On GTA 6 Eve
items.description:
On the eve of GTA 6's official launch on November 19, Sony's PlayStation Network
appears to be facing some issues, at least for some people, at some point,
today. Reports have emerged that the PSN is borked, and although the PlayStation

for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. For now, you can read

items.title: 8BitDo's $49.99 GameCube pad brings classic controls to Switch 2 and PC
items.description:
Controller maker 8BitDo has unveiled the GC Bluetooth Gamepad, a wireless
controller modeled on Nintendo’s GameCube controller, priced at $49.99 and
scheduled to ship December 10. Preorders are open in purple and orange. The pad
works with Nintendo Switch, Switch 2 and Windows and can connect to an original
GameCube with 8BitDo’s separately sold Retro Receiver. The controller keeps the
GameCube’s distinctive button layout and octagonal stick gates while adding
tunnel magnetoresistance (TMR) joysticks, Hall effect triggers and single-rotor
rumble. It costs $20 less than Nintendo’s $69.99 wireless GameCube controller
for Switch 2 and also supports the original Switch and Windows. GameCube games
are available through Switch Online, and the GameCube controller remains in use
in the Super Smash Bros. Melee community. Highlights: Connection options: The
pad supports Bluetooth 5.0, a 2.4GHz wireless USB receiver and wired play over
USB-C. Reported PC connection options are limited to the receiver or cable.
Modern extras: The pad adds a Turbo function and allows multiple controllers to
connect simultaneously. Chat omission: The controller includes a screenshot and
recording button but appears to lack a dedicated C button for Switch 2 GameChat.
Switch Online library: Switch 2's GameCube catalog includes The Legend of Zelda:
The Wind Waker and F-Zero GX. Sources: 8BitDo announce GameCube bluetooth

items.title: KFC Announces GTA 6 Promo Where You Get A Disc-Shaped Piece Of Chicken
items.description:
A lot of people are upset that they can't get GTA 6 on a physical disc, and KFC
is now stepping up to do what Rockstar isn't. KFC Spain has announced a "Replace
the Disc" campaign where customers can get a free disc-shaped piece of fried
chicken when they bring in their GTA 6 box. The promotion takes place December
19 and 20 from 4 to 8 PM at KFC locations in Madrid, Barcelona, Valencia, and
others in the country. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U7_CIIODF0o GTA 6 is sold
at retailers like Best Buy, GameStop, and Target, but the box doesn't include a
disc--instead, you get a code to unlock the game. GTA 6 owner Take-Two recently
reported that 98% of its sales were digital, and while there will be some
physical aspects to gaming forever, it's an increasingly small part of the
business, Take-Two's boss has said. Yum. This is not KFC's only promotion for
GTA 6. KFC Australia is holding a fake funeral for a person named "Ann Alibi" in
Australia's version of Miami on November 19. The fake funeral services are
taking place in the middle of the day, per Ann's wishes, and so that people can
have a "legitimate" reason to take the day off. Numerous brands are latching
onto GTA 6 to leverage the enormity of the game's release to promote their own
stuff. McDonald's, for example, just announced a campaign to get your McNuggets
or Big Mac delivered while you keep playing GTA 6. Even smaller, more regional
brands--including the Massachusetts-based brewery Tree House--have announced GTA
6 promos. GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox
Series X|S. For now, you can read GameSpot's GTA 6 review and check out our GTA
6 guides hub for more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice
City

items.title: How Xbox’s Streaming Deal For GTA 6 Could Expand Its Marketshare By 30%
items.description:
Microsoft and Take-Two recently announced a deal to allow people to stream
Rockstar's GTA 6, and that significantly increases the game's addressable market
on Xbox and means people can play the game for as little as $92. This is
according to a newly issued report from Ampere Analysis, which said the
streaming deal could reach the estimated 10 million "active" Xbox One consoles
out there and expand the total addressable market for GTA 6 on Xbox by 30%. For
anyone just catching up, Microsoft worked out a deal with Take-Two to allow GTA
6 to be streamed to an Xbox console--that could be an Xbox Series X, Xbox Series
S, or even an Xbox One. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAhUXOYNuH4 There are
some key things to know, including how the game streams from an Xbox Series S
version of the game and your streaming experience will depend on the strength
and consistency of your connection. A report from Digital Foundry said the Xbox
Series S edition of GTA 6 struggles with its frame rate at some points, but that
might not be an issue for everyone. No such arrangement is in place for
PlayStation, so the only way to stream GTA 6, at least right now, is on Xbox.
Ampere said there are about 25 million PS4 consoles in the market that are still
active, while Sony is the market leader for current-generation consoles with the
PS5. Why do a deal with Microsoft and not Sony? Ampere said Take-Two was likely
interested in the potential expanded reach with Xbox to help sell more units,
but there might have also been a "direct payment" or a revenue-share agreement
on Xbox that was more preferential to Take-Two. Ampere said Take-Two wants the
PS4 audience as well via streaming, but that might not happen until 2027 at the
soonest, if such a deal ever materializes at all. Beyond this, Ampere said there
could be "technology-based reasons" why Sony didn't get a deal done for GTA 6
streaming. The research firm pointed out how Microsoft is a "hyperscaler" when
it comes to streaming via its vast Azure network, which "puts it in a stronger
position to serve a large influx of users streaming a brand-new game like GTA 6
compared to Sony."  Lucia in GTA 6. "The favorable distribution costs to
Microsoft as the service provider and owner of the cloud infrastructure also
gives it a commercial advantage," Ampere said. "While PS5 users can generally
stream their owned games as long as they have an active PS Plus Premium
subscription, PS4 users don’t have that functionality. Essentially, Sony is not
set up to offer its PS4 users the same streaming experience." Beyond all this,
Ampere highlighted how PS5 users ($731) are spending more than PS4 users ($580)
over the same lifecycle stage of each console. "Converting users to PS5 is more
important to Sony than adding some sales of GTA 6 or PS4 users," Ampere said.
Under $100 to play GTA 6 on Xbox Xbox's streaming deal for GTA 6 also makes Xbox
the most affordable place to play GTA 6. Ampere said the total cost to play on
Xbox could be $92, assuming the player already has an Xbox One, a copy of GTA 6,
a controller, and a screen. Ampere did the math by estimating the cost to be
0.24 cents per hour to stream the game, for a total of $92 via streaming,
assuming a 50-hour runtime for the game. This rate leaves little margin for
Xbox, Ampere said, but the fact that people have to buy streaming time up front
means there will no doubt be "a significant amount of playtime languishing in
accounts that is never used." As announced previously, people can stream GTA 6
to their Xbox console via a Game Pass membership or by purchasing time without a
Game Pass membership. The pricing is below. Cloud playtime packs pricing: 10
hours for $4 25 hours for $8 50 hours for $12 Coinciding with GTA 6's release
and the new streaming deal, Microsoft just instituted limits on how many hours
members can stream before being asked to pay more. These are: Game Pass
Ultimate: 15 hours Game Pass Premium: 10 hours Game Pass Essential: 5 hours Even
beyond the streaming deal, Xbox is the most affordable place to play GTA 6
considering that a new Xbox Series S console costs $500, compared to $600 for
the cheapest new PS5. GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for
PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for
more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

items.title: Magic's Dune Secret Lair adds nine unique cards on November 30
items.description:
Wizards of the Coast has revealed My Arrakis, My Superdrop, a three-part
Dune-themed Secret Lair release for Magic: The Gathering that goes on sale
November 30. The collections contain 20 cards, including nine mechanically
unique designs: eight character cards in Balance of Power and the giant sandworm
Shai-Hulud in Deserts of Arrakis. Prices range from $39.99 to $59.99, and
products are available while supplies last. The collaboration draws on the
recent Dune films, with cards depicting characters including Paul Atreides and
Chani, alongside reimagined Magic cards themed around Arrakis and its spice. The
new cards will not be playable in Standard; Wizards says mechanically unique
Secret Lair cards will eventually appear in official sets. Non-foil versions of
two collections are also expected at game stores later, while foil products and
the Spice collection will be sold through Secret Lair’s online store.
Highlights: Commander angle: All eight Balance of Power character cards are
legendary creatures and potential commanders. Queue timing: The Secret Lair
queue opens one hour before the sale begins. Promo card: Customers who spend at
least $149.99 in one transaction receive a foil Emperor’s Hutment, a Dune-styled
version of Reliquary Tower, while supplies last. Access concerns: GameRant said
the drop is not print-to-demand and warned that Secret Lair queues and scalpers
could make the exclusive new cards difficult for some players to obtain. Getting
to finally make it happen was huge for the team, and we wanted to give fans the
things they have been hoping to see while still finding a few ways to surprise
them. - Matt Hodgins, Director of Secret Lair Sources: Magic Reveals My Arrakis,

items.title: GTA 6 Has A Hilarious Riff On Easter Eggs
items.description:
Now that Rockstar's GTA 6 is available, people are discovering all manner of
things in the game's gigantic open world. One such finding is that GTA 6 has its
own take on Easter eggs, and Rockstar was quite literal. Twitter user xGarbett
posted a video of Jason climbing to the top of a cell tower where there is a
bird's nest with eggs in it. Except these aren't normal eggs. They're painted to
look like Easter eggs, and Jason can throw one of them (with an impressively
tight spiral), sending it hurtling through the air until it crashes down on a
scummy-sounding real estate agent or lawyer of some type. xGarbett said in a
follow-up post that it took about seven minutes to climb the tower, so unlocking
this Easter egg will take some persistence.
https://twitter.com/xGarbett/status/2123088685210202519 Given the scale of GTA
6's world, there are no doubt going to be countless more Easter eggs that
players discover as they make their way through Leonida. Another secret that
players have already discovered is that Bigfoot is back, and he's very smelly.
GTA 6 officially launches for everyone on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series
X|S. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for more details on how
to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

items.title: Bigfoot Is Back In GTA 6, And Apparently He Smells Revolting
items.description:
Grand Theft Auto games have been home to some weird phenomena over the years,
and in GTA 6, it looks like Bigfoot is back and stinkier than ever. As the game
steadily rolls out worldwide--or as people digitally immigrate to New Zealand
for early access--streamers have been posting clips online of their encounters
with the cryptid, and this time, it doesn't look like a man in a suit. It looks
like the Bigfoot sighting is tied to a mission in GTA 6, as the mysterious
creature is wandering the woods of Leonida and it takes off in a panic when you
encounter it. Another clip shows a strange encounter in the woods, with the
player interacting with an effigy that emits noxious fumes and knocks them out.
In a brief cutscene, Bigfoots, uh, really big feet, can be seen approaching
Jason as he drifts in and out of consciousness. In that first clip, Bigfoot is
also covered in a cloud of fumes, which likely references stories about the
mythical creature's potent stench. For GTA--and Red Dead Redemption--fans, this
isn't the first time that they've been involved in a Bigfoot sighting, as
encounters with it stretch back decades. https://youtu.be/4VB7nlJFM9I Back in
2004, rumors began to circulate about Bigfoot existing in GTA: San Andreas, but
Rockstar dismissed these reports as false in 2005. A few years later, in Red
Dead Redemption's Undead Nightmare expansion, protagonist John Marston was
tasked with hunting down a pack of Sasquatches, and it was eventually revealed
that the creatures were peaceful, capable of human speech, and now going extinct
thanks to a certain trigger-happy cowboy. Bigfoot would appear in GTA 5, as
getting 100% completion in the game would unlock a new mission where
co-protagonist Franklin hunts down a creature in Blaine Woods, only to discover
it was a man in a costume. As an extra joke, the Bigfoot impersonator drops a
few references to Red Dead Redemption's infamous encounter, but that doesn't
mean the real Bigfoot isn't lurking in GTA 5. You could use the thermal scope on
the sniper rifle supplied to you to spot a bipedal creature watching you during
the "Predator" mission, and eating a golden Peyote plant under specific
environmental conditions would turn players into Bigfoot. Red Dead Redemption 2
brought an air of mystery back to the Bigfoot mythos, as you could find a
gigantic skeleton half-buried in the snow high up on Mount Shann, and
protagonist Arthur Morgan could also speak to an unseen figure that was heavily
implied to be Bigfoot. Meanwhile, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub for
more details on how to make the most out of your trip to Vice City.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.description:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in
them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to
exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper
agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth, the original
World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent
part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of
possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original
WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.
Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after
Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in
2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling
up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more
likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional
- but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of
updates had previously sanded down. Read more

items.title: Don’t Expect To See Vice City For A Long Time In GTA 6
items.description:
For those still waiting for GTA 6 to unlock, it's possible you have something of
a mistaken impression of what the early hours will look like. Despite partially
sharing a setting with GTA Vice City, you should not expect to be walking up the
game's equivalent of Ocean Drive and Miami Beach in the opening minutes, as in
the 2002 game. Far from it. As we noted in our video discussion on why we gave
GTA 6 a 10/10 in our review, Tamoor and Jake did some expectation-setting.
Rather than starting the game in Vice City, you'll instead spend the opening
hours in a smaller corner of the state of Leonida, Key Lento. Vice City is
undoubtedly the crown jewel of the game's world, but it could be as much as 20
hours before you reach it, depending on how you play. This seems to be a
deliberate decision that, as Tam says, allows you to progress through the world
at roughly the same pace as the ambitions of co-stars Lucia and Jason. The
opening area may not be as glamorous as Vice City, but it is no less detailed
than the rest of the game. It's possible it's only meant to last you around 5-6
hours, but we found it easy to get lost spending far more time than that, which
resulted in Tam not reaching Vice City until after 15 or 16 hours.
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/XkHgrxN3R4g Key Lento provides a good look at how
the game and its simulation work, letting you eventually progress to a much
larger space (seriously, the map is huge) with a good understanding of how
things work. All of this is to say, the glitz and glamor of Vice City are
waiting for you--eventually. To make the most of the opening hours, be sure to
check out our guide on what to do in GTA 6 first.

items.title: Korridor turns those Youtube ads for vertical mobile shooters into a new, "deeply strategic" genre, and I can't decide if it's lying
items.description:
I like to think I'm difficult to hypnotise, but I confess, I'm a sucker for
those Youtube adverts for the mobile vertical shooters. You know the ones:
boglins pour towards an auto-firing player, who must dodge about to grab
upgrades while whittling down the horde. The player in the advert always does
pretty well for 20 seconds, but ahhhh, then they get just a tiny bit
overconfident, mistime how long it'll take them to erode the health of an ogre
midboss, and: bam! Show me one of those ads, and I'll always watch to the end in
the hope that this time, the protagonist will Study The Blade, conquer their
harmatia, and slay the damn ogre. I've never actually played any of the mobile
shooters in question, mind you. I'm far too cultured for that, you dope! Except
that I've just been playing the demo for Korridor, which is supposedly "based
off" of the ads, but might as well be one of the games they're promoting, for
all I know. Read more

items.title: Jason Loves Cats In GTA 6, But Not All Of Them
items.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 co-protagonist Jason is, like many Americans, a fan of cats.
Naturally, being an open-world game with seemingly endless possibilities, GTA 6
does indeed let Jason express that love by petting cats he sees. However, not
every cat is down to be pals with Jason. As shared on social media, if you're
walking around Leonida and spot a friendly-looking cat, you can go give it a
pet. Jason even talks to the cat, because you'd have to be a monster not to, and
the action even gives him a little focus boost.
https://twitter.com/SolutionB2u/status/2123048280959672768 But not all cats are
the same. Another clip shared online shows Jason carjacking someone, as one does
in GTA. After driving away, loud meowing can be heard, and the camera cuts to
inside the car as a cat viciously attacks Jason. A quicktime event is necessary
to get the cat to stop, at which point Jason is able to stop the car and let the
cat out. https://twitter.com/gtasix_/status/2123071228390842498 We can only
imagine what would happen if that were a Rottweiler in the back seat of that car
and not a sort-of-large cat. There are plenty of other animals to kill you while
you're roaming Vice City and the rest of Leonida in Grand Theft Auto 6, and most
of those would be less embarrassing to mention in your obituary than "cat."
Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the most expansive and detailed games ever made,
and if you're looking for some help, you can check out our GTA 6 guides hub as
well as our guide on what to do first. In GameSpot's GTA 6 review, Tamoor
Hussain said, "This game is the culmination of everything the developer has
previously achieved in the open-world space that pushes the genre to heights
that, in all likelihood, no other developer will be able to reach. GTA 6 is an
astonishing open-world action game that I'd wager won't be outdone until Grand
Theft Auto 7," ultimately awarding it a 10/10 score.

items.title: How Long Does It Take To Fly Across The Entire GTA 6 Map?
items.description:
The Grand Theft Auto 6 map is absolutely massive, gigantic, and at least one
more synonym to encapsulate its size accurately. Whether it's land, sea, or air,
covering it is going to take a lot of time, but just how many hours should you
set aside for a flight across Leonida? We found out for ourselves by piloting a
single-propeller plane across the map, which took us an entire four minutes and
10 seconds between the two points on the map. That's pretty big!
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/VHLzkTAAb74?feature=share We've known for a while
that the GTA 6 map was going to be big--with roughly more playable space than
GTA 4, GTA 5, and Red Dead Redemption 2 combined--but even that claim doesn't
put into perspective just how enormous the game truly is until you experience it
for yourself. Another fascinating tidbit is that escaping GTA 6 is
nigh-impossible, but definitely worth attempting. As one streamer has
discovered, if you try to cheese it on water using a jet ski, you'll run out of
fuel and be left stranded in the water. There might be a happy ending to this
scenario, as some streamers have posted clips of a dog on a wave runner coming
to their rescue. We've tried to replicate this ourselves, but we've had no luck
yet. But if you choose to stay within Leonida's invisible boundaries, you won't
run out of things to do for quite some time. Between missions to improve your
lot in life, pursue relationship goals, and soak up the scenery, the reactive
open world of GTA 6 will keep you entertained for hours. Our GTA 6 review gave
the game a rare 10/10 score, and dozens of other reviewers worldwide have also
been very impressed with what Rockstar Games has achieved. You can experience
all of that for yourself soon, and if you're not planning to do some digital
tourism with a long walk, check out our GTA 6 guides hub for all kinds of
walkthroughs to help you survive and thrive in the game.

items.title: Rockstar Founder Issues Rare Statement As GTA 6 Launches To Superb Reviews And Huge Sales
items.description:
We might not hear from him much, but Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser remains
highly involved with the studio and its games, and that includes GTA 6, which is
available now in New Zealand and everywhere else on November 19. To mark the
game's launch, Houser released a statement in which he said Rockstar has once
again tried to create a game in GTA 6 that "exceeds your expectations" and shows
"what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special."
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAhUXOYNuH4 He told GamesRadar: "Rockstar Games
was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all
other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be
thought of as stories and worlds that live on with us." The executive went on to
say that he hopes GTA 6 feels "both familiar and entirely new," and above all
else, something that people find to be fun. "This is a narrative set in a world
of possibilities--and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately
feels, and concludes," he added. Finally, Houser reminded people that GTA 6
might be the pinnacle of the franchise so far, but Rockstar isn't closing up
shop anytime soon. "We look forward to many more years of sharing these
experiences with you," he said. It's possible it won't be another 13 years for
the next GTA game, as Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, has said the "nature and
velocity" of GTA releases will change. Sam Houser rarely releases statements,
gives interviews, or appears in Rockstar's promotional efforts, so even this
celebratory statement is notable. GQ writer Sam White recently posted a series
of tweets (and then deleted them) saying an interview he had planned with Sam
Houser fell apart at the last minute. On GTA 6, Sam Houser was involved in every
aspect of the game's creative process. Sam Houser's brother, Dan Houser, left
Rockstar in 2020 after the successful launch of Red Dead Redemption II. He
started a new company, Absurd Ventures, which is working on an open-world comedy
game that will be revealed soon. GTA 6 arrives for everyone on November 19, and
it's expected to be a massive success, the likes of which the industry hasn't
seen since ... 2013's GTA 5. In GameSpot's GTA 6 review, Tamoor Hussain said
there might not be another game like it until the inevitable GTA 7.

items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.description:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r, or Driver 3, or my personal favourite
Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous
bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the
accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off
car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized
tupperware container. A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there
was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the
opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact
be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and
even 22 years before GTA 6's idolising reviews, that was no small promise;
Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see
San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have
Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world,
either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were
about to wheel into the showroom. You likely know the rest, though one of the
dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this
case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having
recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the
possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell
you: it was. Read more

items.title: GTA 6’s Platinum trophy may demand up to 200 hours
items.description:
Rockstar’s Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on
Nov. 19, and its trophy and achievement lists outline the requirements for full
completion. Earning the Platinum trophy could take up to 200 hours, according to
estimates. The main story alone is expected to take roughly 70 to 80 hours for
many players, though reported playthroughs range from 42 hours to 115. The
Platinum requires 100% completion, but players do not have to finish every
activity or collect everything. After the story, an in-game checklist tracks
progress, and players can return to Leonida to complete the remaining
requirements at their own pace. Highlights: Selective checklist: The completion
checklist asks players to scan 200 of 277 base-model vehicles and study 100 of
255 animals, rather than catalog every vehicle or species. Activity targets:
Other goals include completing 70 of 80 challenges, winning 30 unique races,
earning 42 shooting-range gold medals and completing 300 stunts. Trophy count:
The PlayStation list has 55 trophies—one Platinum, two Gold, six Silver and 46
Bronze—while Xbox’s achievement list totals 1,000 Gamerscore. Cloud option: Xbox
announced that owners of Xbox One consoles can stream the game through Xbox
Cloud Gaming from launch, without installing a native Xbox One version. Sources:

items.title: Rockstar launches GTA 6 worldwide after 13-year wait
items.description:
Rockstar Games launched Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and
Xbox Series X|S, returning the series to Vice City and the fictional state of
Leonida. The release follows 2013’s Grand Theft Auto V. Rockstar president and
co-founder Sam Houser said the studio aimed to show what games can achieve as a
storytelling medium. Reviews published before launch put the game at or near the
top of all-time critics’ rankings; 80 Level reported more than 140 review scores
and a Metacritic ranking above The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Rockstar
leaders described a design built around more flexible missions and a large world
intended to support future additions. The company has not announced a new GTA
Online service or confirmed single-player expansions. Players in New Zealand and
Australia received access ahead of the November 19 launch in other territories.
Highlights: China access: Rockstar promoted the game on Douyin, China’s version
of TikTok, although GTA 6 was absent from the country’s list of approved
imported games and has no official sales authorization there. Rosario ban: A
Rosario councillor proposed repealing the city’s 1998 prohibition on exhibiting
and selling GTA titles; the measure was still in force for GTA 6’s release.
Perspectives: Warren Spector, creator of Deus Ex: Spector congratulated the
development team but argued that other studios should not copy the game’s
reported billion-dollar development budget. He said he would prefer many games
and broader employment to one exceptionally expensive production. (GamesRadar+)
Nestor Uriarte, Rockstar animation programmer: Uriarte argued that collective
representation could give workers a voice in decisions about generative
artificial intelligence, warning that the technology risks devaluing creative
skills and replacing workers. (Rock Paper Shotgun) Sources: Rockstar Games

items.title: The GTA 6 Map Is Truly, Truly Massive (Of Course)
items.description:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and Rockstar Games has released the
game's official map. It is absolutely gigantic. Even though we knew the GTA 6
map would be big--it has more playable space than GT4, GTA 5, and Red Dead
Redemption 2 combined--seeing the map for yourself shows off its truly
gargantuan scale. Behold, the GTA 6 map. As confirmed previously, GTA 6 takes
place in the state of Leonida, which is a stand-in for Florida. The central hub
is Vice City itself (GTA's version of Miami), but the game takes players well
beyond that to numerous surrounding counties. GameSpot's GTA 6 review scored the
game a rare 10/10. “GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game that I’d
wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7,” reviewer Tamoor Hussain said.
GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to become the
highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and is tied with
the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score ever. After
GTA 6 reviews came online, shares of Rockstar owner Take-Two ripped higher, but
the company is still down massively this year and over the past 12 months. For
more, check out GameSpot's Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

items.title: GTA 6 Owner Take-Two’s Stock Adds Billions After Rave Reviews, But It’s Not All Good News
items.description:
After more than 10 years of waiting, Rockstar's GTA 6 is finally available now
(at least in New Zealand and Australia). The anticipation has been sky-high for
both consumers and investors alike, and Rockstar's owner, Take-Two, is seeing a
huge uplift in its share price today after the game's overwhelmingly positive
reviews landed. Take-Two shares rose by nearly7% in pre-market trading today,
and moved higher from there as the day went on. This meant that Take-Two's
market cap grew by billions today alone. Stock analysts expected share value to
increase in the lead-up to launch, and many expect it to go higher still due to
the expected launches of GTA Online and a PC edition of the game in 2027.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ftI6gjFsPuw&t=1s While Take-Two's stock price is
popping today, Take-Two remains down close to 20% so far in 2026 and is down
about 15% over the past 12 months. Why? No one really knows, because the stock
market is fickle. Take-Two's stock price got hammered earlier this year when
Google announced new AI software to make games, presumably spooking investors.
The stock has not recovered since. The 52-week high for Take-Two is $265.65, and
the 52-week low is $183.86. Zooming further out, though, Take-Two has been a
fantastic investment for people who bought and held for a long time. As Rand
Group points out, $10,000 invested into Take-Two when GTA 5 launched in 2013 has
grown to more than $120,000 today.
https://twitter.com/randgroup/status/2123139175881019530 GameSpot's GTA 6 review
scored the game a rare 10/10. "GTA 6 is an astonishing open-world action game
that I’d wager won’t be outdone until Grand Theft Auto 7," reviewer Tamoor
Hussain said. GTA 6 has now unseated the Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 to
become the highest-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site, Metacritic, and
is tied with the original Ocarina of Time for the highest aggregate review score
ever. For more on GTA 6, including preload information, preorder bonuses, and
release times, check out our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

items.title: Rockstar rules out 40fps and 60fps modes for GTA 6 on consoles
items.description:
Rockstar Games says Grand Theft Auto 6 will not get 40- or 60-frame-per-second
modes on current consoles, including Sony’s PlayStation 5 Pro, as the game
launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The studio says simulating the
game’s densely populated world, Leonida, requires too much processing power to
support higher frame rates without reducing simulation or visual detail.
Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers said the Pro’s stronger
graphics processor and image-upscaling features improve visual quality, but its
central processor is only slightly faster than the base PS5’s and cannot run the
game simulation at a higher rate. Senior vice president of technology Jonathon
Ashcroft said the team chose 30fps to balance simulation, presentation and
gameplay within a roughly 33-millisecond frame budget. Digital Foundry’s testing
found that the PS5 Pro maintains 30fps most consistently, while the base PS5 and
Xbox Series X can dip below that target in demanding scenes; the Xbox Series S
has more frequent drops. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, so it is
unclear whether higher frame rates will be available on that platform.
Highlights: Resolution: PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X render at 1440p before
upscaling to 4K; Xbox Series S renders at 720p and uses AMD FSR 4 to upscale to
1080p. Variable refresh rate (VRR): Wccftech says Xbox Series X can feel
slightly smoother than the base PS5 because its 120Hz VRR mode works at the
game’s frame rates; PS5’s system-level VRR does not engage below 48fps. Input
response: Rockstar vice president of technology David Hynd said the team removed
a full frame of input delay compared with earlier games by sampling controller
input as late as possible and trimming pauses at the start of animations. Frame
interpolation: An experimental PC streaming tool called SmoovPlay generated up
to 120 displayed frames per second from PS5 footage, but it does not increase
the game’s underlying 30fps response rate and adds latency. Critical response:
IGN awarded the game 10/10, while Polygon’s review said the 30fps cap had a
negligible effect on the reviewer’s experience because performance remained
smooth most of the time. Perspectives: Rockstar Games: Co-studio head and head
of development Rob Nelson said a higher-frame-rate mode would require
unacceptable compromises to the game’s design. (IGN) Digital Foundry: Analyst
John Linneman described GTA 6 as the smoothest Grand Theft Auto game at launch,
while stressing that whether the 30fps trade-off is worthwhile depends on each
player. (GamesRadar+) Frame-rate-focused players: Some players criticized the
30fps cap after expecting a performance option on modern consoles. (Polygon)

items.title: Clair Obscur lead writer leaves Sandfall, plans narrative funding initiative
items.description:
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead narrative designer on the award-winning role-playing
game Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, left developer Sandfall Interactive in July
after finishing her work on the game, she said in an interview released after
she won a BAFTA Breakthrough U.S. award. She has not explained why the two sides
parted ways. She plans to write her own stories and develop a fund to help
emerging game writers and narrative-led studios secure early backing and
mentorship. Svedberg-Yen says many developers treat story as something to add
late in development. She argues that integrating narrative from the outset can
shape a game’s other disciplines. The fund would help creators produce demos to
attract publishers and could include an incubation program; she says it is
intended to work with publishers, not replace them. Sandfall has not announced
its next project, and Svedberg-Yen will not be involved in its future work. The
studio has said its creative direction will follow its own taste. Highlights:
People and conditions: Svedberg-Yen called for better investment in creative
workers, saying developers should be paid properly and receive health care and
vacations. The strongest feeling in me right now for 2027 is I want to help. -
Jennifer Svedberg-Yen, lead narrative designer of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33

investment should prioritize and protect creative workers, rather than focus

items.title: MindsEye studio seeks lawsuit proceeds to repay £61.7 million debt
items.description:
Build a Rocket Boy, the developer of action game MindsEye, owes £61.7 million
and is pursuing legal claims against several third parties it alleges helped
coordinate negative online reviews of the game. The company’s administrators say
any recovery is uncertain, but describe the litigation as potentially the
largest asset available to repay creditors. The largest reported debt is about
£36.4 million to Chinese gaming company NetEase. Build a Rocket Boy entered
administration in September 2026 after failing to secure further investment for
development, and its directors have sought additional outside funding to cover
legal costs. The administrators are assessing the claims and how best to
preserve or realize their value; the documents do not identify all the parties
being sued. Highlights: Debt breakdown: The filing lists about £4.2 million owed
to Diameter Dislocation Master Fund and more than £1.1 million owed to founder
Leslie Benzies. Company allegations: Build a Rocket Boy co-CEO Mark Gerhard
alleged that a “very big American company” spent more than €1 million in 2025 on
criminal activity against the studio. He also named UK influencer agency Ritual
Network, three unnamed journalists and some studio employees as alleged
participants. Game reception: Tweakers reported Metacritic averages of 39/100
from critics and 2.7/10 from players. Earlier funding: Build a Rocket Boy had
raised more than £233 million in investment by 2024, including a $110 million
Series D round, according to company documents cited by IGN. People had their
hands on the scale and deliberately tried to shape a negative narrative around
the product - Mark Gerhard, Build a Rocket Boy co-CEO Perspectives: Ritual
Network: The UK influencer agency denied allegations that it orchestrated a paid
campaign to damage MindsEye's reputation. (IGN) Former Build a Rocket Boy
employee: A former employee told GamesIndustry.biz they blamed the studio's
leaders, rather than saboteurs, for the company's looming collapse.
(GamesIndustry.biz) Sources: Despite being £61.7 million in debt, bankrupt

items.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 review
items.description:
My best attempt at summing up Grand Theft Auto 6 came from a conversation with a
friend about something else entirely. This friend was telling me about a theory
they'd recently heard, and half agreed with, that just so happened to layer over
this game perfectly. Americans, they said, paraphrasing, have found a new 'third
place': the car. Read more

items.title: GTA VI sets livestream record as critics praise its open world
items.description:
Grand Theft Auto VI drew a record 7,886,402 concurrent viewers across
livestreaming platforms as it became available in New Zealand ahead of its
worldwide release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. Reviewers praised the
game’s detailed, reactive world and the relationship between its two leads,
Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. Its Metacritic average reached 99, matching The
Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Some reviewers questioned whether the game’s
realism and greater consequences for players’ actions dull the freewheeling
chaos of earlier entries, while others praised its chases and character-driven
story. The game is available on current PlayStation and Xbox consoles, but not
yet on PC. Players have begun finding hidden locations linked to fan theories,
including a house in Leonida that matches an image from the 2021 San Andreas
remaster. The livestreaming audience set its record before the game was
available in most markets. Highlights: Fan discovery: Inside the Leonida house
matching an image from the 2021 San Andreas remaster, players found a conspiracy
theorist’s notes about nonplayer characters, the state’s borders, and Jason and
Lucia. Network surge: New Zealand provider Chorus recorded 5.6 terabits per
second of network traffic during the download rush, topping its previous 5.4
Tbps peak set by Fortnite in February 2025. Their motivations and goals are very
different from the main characters of previous GTA games, and their priority is
really about escape rather than revenge or empire building. - Luke Reilly, IGN
reviewer Perspectives: Players posting on social media: Some early players
criticized the 30-fps performance and slower, routine activities, contrasting
their experience with the largely glowing critic reception. (LiveMint) Game
streamers: Some creators told IGN they expect the game to provide material for
months or years, while others thought its streaming appeal could last only a few
weeks. (IGN) Sources: GTA 6 review: the most complete open-world experience

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever sets 15-year weekly player record
items.description:
World of Warcraft: Forever, Blizzard’s new version of its massively multiplayer
online role-playing game, has more weekly players than any World of Warcraft
release in 15 years, executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale said
on Nov. 18. The game launched Nov. 4, and Blizzard has also called it the
series’ biggest launch by peak concurrent players. Its latest figures include
more than 15 million characters created, nearly 1.5 billion quests completed,
almost 29 million player-versus-player kills and nearly 197 million player
deaths. Forever reworks the original game world with new content while retaining
its level-60 cap. A German review praised its updated classes, convenience
features and new adventures, while noting that lengthy travel and repetitive
gathering quests remain. Blizzard plans more quests, dungeons, raids and
player-versus-player content. As of Nov. 18, the first raids were still about
three weeks away. Highlights: Character counts: The 15-million figure counts
characters, not distinct players. A player can create multiple characters on one
account, and Blizzard has not published an exact player total. New adventures:
The game adds more than 1,000 quests, nine new five-player dungeons and updated
areas including Hyjal, Shen'dralas and the Riverlands. Classic balance: The
review says Forever keeps the original leveling pace and avoids flying mounts
and automatic dungeon teleports to preserve atmosphere and social play. Launch
activity: Players have formed more than 71 million parties and over 140,000
guilds and defeated nearly 9.8 billion enemies. Sources: WoW: Forever Weekly
Player Numbers Are The Highest For Blizzard’s MMO In 15 Years - gamespot.com
WoW: Forever "has more people playing weekly" than Blizzard's seen in 15 years,
lead says - gamesradar.com WoW: Forever is huge: Players have created over 15
million characters so far - pcgamer.com World Of Warcraft: Forever Just Broke A
15-Year-Old Record - kotaku.com World of Warcraft: Forever im Test – zurück in
die Zukunft! - computerbild.de
items.content:
World of Warcraft: Forever, Blizzard’s new version of its massively multiplayer
online role-playing game, has more weekly players than any World of Warcraft
release in 15 years, executive producer and vice president Holly Longdale said
on Nov. 18. The game launched Nov. 4, and Blizzard has also called it the
series’ biggest launch by peak concurrent players. Its latest figures include
more than 15 million characters created, nearly 1.5 billion quests completed,
almost 29 million player-versus-player kills and nearly 197 million player
deaths. Forever reworks the original game world with new content while retaining
its level-60 cap. A German review praised its updated classes, convenience
features and new adventures, while noting that lengthy travel and repetitive
gathering quests remain. Blizzard plans more quests, dungeons, raids and
player-versus-player content. As of Nov. 18, the first raids were still about
three weeks away.

A screenshot of the World of Warcraft: Forever beta. Two Skyborne elves stand in
a grove.

 * Classic balance: The review says Forever keeps the original leveling pace and
   avoids flying mounts and automatic dungeon teleports to preserve atmosphere
   and social play.
 * Launch activity: Players have formed more than 71 million parties and over
   140,000 guilds and defeated nearly 9.8 billion enemies.

items.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success
items.description:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft
Auto. Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't
GTA 6, which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making,
with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network
of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open
world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game
productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel
mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial
production shadowed by labour disputes, that appears to have given Rockstar's
various teams little time or space to think about anything else. It wasn't ever
thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a
considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption. Once upon a time, they had a
reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former
Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent,
the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on
Grand Theft Auto 5. Read more

items.title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI
items.description:
As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union
have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI,
Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a
manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the
workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike. The manifesto states
that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games
they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done
to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment,
the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as
wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.
Read more

items.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
items.description:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your
understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering
puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics,
broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics, together with more
recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus. Resources come in,
and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before
sliding them into an output hopper. The difference is that you're doing this
inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a
largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the
refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid
rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can
manufacture anything. Read more

items.description:
Split-screen multiplayer is often treated by developers as a forgotten vestige
of a bygone age, something to be left behind as the standardisation of online
play makes it redundant, especially following the pandemic. It's considered
unlikely that you'll have another human being in your home to pick up a
controller with you, and since you've inevitably got an internet connection, why

beauty in playing something shoulder to shoulder on a couch with another person,
and it seems Fuse Games sees that light too, with Star Wars: Galactic Racer set
to be updated to add local splitscreen multiplayer sometime early next year.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is GTA 5 without the finesse - so why is the 2004 classic such a strange delight to return to?
items.description:
There is a place in Whitewood Estates where a promising stretch of blacktop
suddenly gives way to the desert. It feels like the road has been erased, a
sentence left unfinished. It's quietly strange, a weird bit of urban
wrongfooting. But I guess it makes some kind of sense. California, after all, is
home to California City, a town that was planned and then never really built. It
sits out there now, north of Los Angeles, streets laid out but slowly being
eaten by the sand and dirt. Still, 14,000 people lived there as of 2018. Design
limitation or something stranger, this digital dead end is a reminder that all
of this land, so modern, so ancient - all of this is spook country. Read more

items.title: Microsoft's SideWinder Strategic Commander was a failed attempt to reimagine RTS controls. 23 years later, why are some players still using it?
items.description:
PC players have been conditioned for decades to accept the keyboard-and-mouse
setup for RTS games. One hand has to handle movement and commands through a
keyboard, while the other points, drags, and selects with a mouse. Peripheral
makers have, usually with the addition of more buttons, made many minor
variations to this time-honored arrangement, but there's only ever been one real
attempt to rethink it entirely for the PC: the Microsoft SideWinder Strategic
Commander. Read more

items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
items.description:
New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly
draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed,
not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have
given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all
exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that
reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. Deign to
slap somebody's hand, and they'll pop into colour and be able to join you for
various activities. For example, going fishing, playing instruments round the
campfire, playing dress-up and pulling emotes in group photos, bouncing around
on strangely inflated yaks, or questing forth to heal troubled spirits. There's
some material gathering and crafting, and there are recurring storms that make
the ambience more threatening, but overcoming a challenge doesn't feel like the
point of Spirit Crossing. The "missions" are just an excuse to hang out
together. Read more

items.title: My murderous wine merchant whines for a chance at republican rule in Crusader Kings 3’s Silk and Silver expansion, which isn't only about the money
items.description:
The tentacles of my trade empire snake up towards France in the west, down
towards Africa in the south, and off into Hungary in the east. Yet, I still
can’t reach out and grasp the throne that sits right in front of me. I’m Marco
Sanudo, and the throne of the serene republic of Venice eludes me. I’ve shed
blood in its name, the blood of someone else named Marco no less. I’ve managed
to avoid punishment for that crime, despite the fact it earned me a fiefdom to
rule while I’ve tried to up my patrician score enough to be the lucky party the
next time a ruling Doge dies in office (or runs out their 10 year term). Sadly,
Doge Leonardo, the mysterious masked lord who’s had an iron grip on power since
the first couple of old blokes to hold the position in this playthrough popped

items.title: Intel are being sued for "misleading" investors about "a massive glut of unwanted PC inventory" thanks to AI-fuelled price hikes
items.description:
Tech giant Intel are being taken to court for allegedly "misleading" their
investors about the sheer scale of the impact of generative AI-fuelled component
price hikes on PC sales. The class action lawsuit in question claims that
Intel's distribution and manufacturing partners have had to deal with "a massive
glut of unwanted PC inventory", and that the gains from Intel's investments in
AI datacenters aren't enough to make up for slowing sales of PCs to regular
Josephines who just want fancy boxes they can play Deadlock on. All this follows
Intel's last round of quarterly results, in which they announced a significant
revenue fall; this triggered an Intel stock price drop from $92.07 per share on
October 29th to $65.76 per share the next day, which this week's lawsuit
characterises as "the largest single-day price decline for Intel common stock in
over 50 years". Read more

items.title: The Sunday Papers
items.description:
While following a peculiar trail of silver and saffron leaves around the largest
roots of the Treehouse, you come across a hexagonal wooden door lying
half-hidden among ivy and moss. Scraping away the dirt, you discover a faint,
absurd engraving of a newspaper. What mystery is here? You turn the brass knob –
strange, it is warm! – and the engraving of the newspaper flutters. The pages
turn faster and faster, emitting a howling gale that bowls you head over foot.
When you pick yourself up, you are inside a vast attic full of books and
bricabrac, lit from one side by windows that offer no view of the outside world
– just light and mist. Tarnation! You have been lured into the eternal prison of
Sunday Afternoon. Fortunately, there are several ways to escape. Each of the
arcane objects before you is secretly a portal, transporting you to another site
of arcane activity, in a bizarre web of diversions that cannot possibly reflect
the hand of a human curator. Which will you choose? Read more

As we teeter on the brink of gaming's biggest launch of 2026 - perhaps even
decade - so many questions swirl: which GTA 6 cars will make the best vrrrrm? Is
it possible for me to be any more obsessed with that Justice theme song? On a
scale of one to ten, how many dongs? Answers will inevitably come, but for now -
as we crank up the Phil Collins and roar deeper into Eurogamer's GTA Week -
there's only one question we're concerned with. Yes, it's the return of our
irregular series The Big Question, in which we ponder another topical talking
point before wafting it lovingly over to you. And this time around we're asking,
what's the best GTA? Read more

items.title: Forage and fight for ingredients in a magical 1960s Italy and whip up some tasty meals Cooking Mama style in The Snackbar at the End of the World
items.description:
If a game is about cooking, at minimum I'll have to give it a quick testspin.
Outside of this whole writing about video games thing, my other lot in life is
soul bound to food, so I'm always curious to see how the two can be mixed
together. And earlier this week, The Snackbar at the End of the World was
revealed, a wonderfully cartoonish action-adventure game set in a magical,
slightly post-apocalyptic version of 1960s Italy where you go out and forage for
ingredients while fending off monstrous crops before turning them into tasty
meals back in your struggling restaurant. Read more

items.title: Rasen, out in early access now, is a PvP focused take on Dark Souls that borrows one of fighting games' best techy tricks
items.description:
The idea of Dark Souls PvP has always scared me a tad. You can replace Dark
Souls with Bloodborne or Elden Ring, I've typically just been a coward when it
comes to the idea of fighting another, real person. They're probably going to be
better than me! I don't use tactics in Souls games, I use brute force until I
get my way! That being said, I do have to admit I quite like the look of Rasen,
a game that is essentially just the PvP component of Dark Souls (or PvE if you
just want to take on some computer-controlled enemies) that just launched into
early access. Read more

items.title: Congratulations to people who feel mean shooting random NPCs, because GTA 6 tries "to provide mechanisms that encourage" empathy
items.description:
When you think about GTA as a series, the first thing that probably comes to
mind is driving through crowds of people, gunning down whoever you like, just
generally doing crime without any care in the world. I wouldn't exactly call it
an empathy game, not to say that other games are any better at such a thing
anyway. But with GTA 6 out, crikey, next bloody week, a new interview has gone
up with co-studio head Rob Nelson where he shared that you have a bit more space
to be empathetic compared to previous entries. Read more

items.title: Vice City was the GTA that established Rockstar's killer formula - and 24 years on, it's still one of the best games ever made
items.description:
"Get the limey out of here," Burt Reynolds tells the producers of GTA: Vice City
during a recording session for the game, as Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser
enters the studio. "I'm not going to work if this limey Brit is in here!" Houser
refuses to leave, so the story goes - he just came down to meet one of his
heroes! - and he and Reynolds end up chest-to-chest, about to come to blows,
before a studio engineer breaks up the fight. Read more

items.title: While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure
items.description:
Declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my
favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and
their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and
Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them.
The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like
Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight
hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.
Read more

items.title: Worst Class Ever takes asymmetrical multiplayer back to school, with a teacher player trying to spot the naughty children among the NPCs
items.description:
What's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went
to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any
injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave
anybody with years of mental distress. I'll start: I once had to write a
four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being
caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three
pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The
teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he
would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine. Read
more

items.title: How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games
items.description:
Much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers,
Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and
helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort
of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday,
anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of
footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's
base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and
Bunurong Boon Wurrung land. When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming
body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically
redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics,
intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections
where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an
expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving
elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori
voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and
square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone. Read more

items.title: Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes
items.description:
Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand
laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a
million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare
alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in
my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god,
they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome
our new galactic overlords!" But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live
newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in
which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in
the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic
system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a
very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a
miniature blackhole. Read more

items.description:

items.title: Amid soaring PC hardware prices, gaming monitors are getting cheaper and cheaper. Here's why, and what to buy
items.description:
Hello, good local-time-zone-adjusted afternoon, and let's just say it's been a
while. But I come back to you now at the turn of the technological tide. Well,
sort of. Sadly I'm not here to predict an end to the ridiculous AI-fuelled chip
crisis. That whole mess has a couple of years to run, surely. Instead I speak of
screens, where there is actually some very good news. In short, have you seen
how cheap PC gaming monitors are? I mean remarkably, almost stupendously, cheap.
I'm talking £60 / $60 for an entry-level 1080p panel with triple-digit refresh
rate, sub-£200 / $250 for high-refresh 4K gaming. Heck, even OLED monitors now
start with a "2" in both currencies. Read more

items.title: After being laid off by Microsoft, former Doom devs found new Smash TV-influenced FPS studio that isn't "subject to investor demands"
items.description:
Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as
part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a
new employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a
single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and
dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an
influence on Smash TV. Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books,
including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin
Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis,
senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke,
and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of
old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words. Read
more

items.title: Minerva Rising is a Frostpunk-meets-Silo underground city builder in which rebel citizens can hack your camera
items.description:
Minerva Rising is a post-apocalyptic city builder in which your city extends
deep underground, divided into levels with their own resources, industries, and
communities. You are an artificial intelligence with overall control, but watch
out: if you alienate the population of any particular level by, say, forgetting
to supply them with oxygen, subversives may rise up and cut your feed, blinding
you to their activities. I'm keen to know whether it's possible for every level
to lose faith in you and hack your cameras, reducing the game to a pile of
"SIGNAL NOT FOUND" messages. I'm also imagining turning the feeds back on and
discovering that everybody is having a massive orgy. Stupid sexy vault dwellers!
You'll go forth and multiply when Deep Thought tells you to, and not a second
before. Read more

items.title: There were 47 graphics chip makers in 1998. Where did they all go?
items.description:
Some may find this hard to believe, given the absolute state of the market
today, but if you were building a gaming PC in 1998, the hard part wasn’t
finding somewhere that had 3D cards in stock for a reasonable price. It was
choosing the right one among a glut of potential, reasonably affordable options.
In 1998, 47 companies were designing or selling PC graphics, driving a market
that hit 130 million units and outsold PCs themselves. Just two years later, at
the turn of the new millennium, only 15 remained, and not long after that, there
were merely two: Nvidia and ATI, nowadays part of AMD. Read more

items.title: Keeping hold of Company of Heroes was essential for Relic to leave Sega, Relic CEO says – "Without it we would have been a dead studio"
items.description:
In the nearly 30 years since they opened their doors, Relic have been an
enormously influential studio. Responsible for lauded RTS series Homeworld, Dawn
of War, and Company of Heroes, they also dabbled in other genres with
third-person shooter The Outfit and the original Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine.
Yet, despite this history, in 2024, when Relic were negotiating their sale from
Sega to UK investment firm Emona Capita, CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights
to Company of Heroes had to be part of the deal. "Without it we would have been
a dead studio," he tells me. Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that
there are "numerous examples" of studios that weren't able to survive on their
name alone. Not only did Relic need the ability to make more games in the series
that they were known for, but they also needed the income from back catalogue
sales a series like Company of Heroes provides. Read more

[https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/sega-sells-company-of-heroes-developer-relic-and-lays-off-more-staff-at-creative-assembly-and-hardlight],
CEO Justin Dowdeswell knew the rights to Company of Heroes had to be part of the
deal. "Without it we would have been a dead studio," he tells me.

Without naming names Dowdeswell points out that there are "numerous examples" of
studios that weren't able to survive on their name alone. Not only did Relic
need the ability to make more games in the series that they were known for, but
they also needed the income from back catalogue sales a series like Company of
Heroes provides.

Read more

items.title: "A fight for all workers": SAG-AFTRA throw weight behind emerging Rockstar union ahead of its GTA 6 release week vote
items.description:
In what has come to feel like the dawn of the final day before Grand Theft Auto
VI's release, one thing that Rockstar really don't want people to be aware of is
the ongoing legal dispute between the Rockstar Games Workers Union and the
studio itself following Rockstar's alleged union busting in firing 31 union
members last year. Starting on the 12th through to the 26th, recognition of the
union will be voted upon by staff to ensure that workers would be given a say
over "topics including pay and bonuses, overtime, redundancies, flexible working
arrangements, and generative AI policies." If it passes, the vote would also
make the union the largest recognised union in the UK games industry, partly
thanks to its partnership with the Independent Workers Union of Great Britain.
Now, the global labor union SAG-AFTRA have chimed in to endorse the Workers
Union, offering solidarity to the members involved and granting important
leverage from a global force. Read more

items.title: Don't be fooled by Horses of Hoofprint Bay's hand-drawn art, this stable management game has all the drama of a Jilly Cooper novel
items.description:
Poema is my pride and joy. She was my first horse and she's a competition
winner, but she's reached her potential. She'll never be a show jumper, and
that's where the money and prestige are to be found. If I'm ever to grow my
horse farm into a nationally renowned equestrian centre, I need the cash to
expand and upgrade my facilities. Poema is a hoofstep on the path to that
future, but she's not going to be able to take me all the way herself. For all
its hand-drawn aesthetics, Horses of Hoofprint Bay has hard realities like the
limits of Poema's future bubbling under its surface. While the game's scripted
narrative may be lacking, it's shockingly easy to fill in the gaps with drama
worthy of a Jilly Cooper novel. Read more

items.title: Cyberattack on Sega third-party newsletter distributor reportedly sees over two million email addresses leaked, but Sega accounts unaffected

cyberattack on Japanese email delivery provider Arara, whom the Like A Dragon

affected the Sega accounts you can use receive in-game rewards and access a

urged those who signed up for the affected newsletters to be wary of potential
phishing attempts. Read more

items.title: Microsoft workers accuse company of trying to get customers "addicted" to AI while forcing it on their own staff and making them party to "human rights violations"
items.description:
A group of "concerned Microsoft workers" have published an open letter
criticising their employer's "speed-at-all-costs" approach to generative AI,
which they argue is "harming our customers, colleagues, shareholders, vendors,
and the planet". They accuse Microsoft leadership of trying to get people
"addicted" to genAI, while making their own staff miserable by mandating AI
usage. Echoing the on-going BDS campaign against Microsoft's Xbox business, the
writers contend that Microsoft have become party to "human rights violations" by
selling generative AI technology to Israel's military during the latter's
invasion of Gaza, which a UN commission has deemed a genocide. They're also
critical of Microsoft's contracts with the USA's draconian Immigration and
Customs Enforcement agency. While seemingly not against generative AI in
principle, they're organising against "the AI industry’s trajectory to continue
to enrich AI’s powerful few", pointing out that AI companies now account for a
terrifying share of the global stock market. Read more

items.title: "The lesson learned is you can have both": Skyrim lead designer reckons there's merit in Baldur's Gate 3-style tough choices and Bethesda's do-anything approach
items.description:
Whether RPGs are better off prioritising player freedom or endeavouring to have
several doors slam shut every time you put another foot forwards in order to
encourage multiple runs with different characters is, to put it bluntly,
something I reckon will still be a matter of debate in the year 4000. We'll all
have evolved in non-corporeal beings floating in a galaxy that's been racked by
such change that even the six million copies of The Elder Scrolls 5 we've
littered the Earth with will have been swept away into the great recycling bin
on the gods' desktop, and there'll still be sniping going on about whether it's
ok that Skyrim lets you be a master thiefssassin who leads the companions, knows
every spell under the sun, and slapped up a world-eating dragon for fun. For
what it's worth, the game's lead designer reckons both games that do and don't
let you do that have their merits when executed well. Read more

admitting in an extraordinary public statement that he was "unfaithful to my
wife." Still, the two investigations are likely to start a bizarre new leg in
the alread-messy AI arms race that the US and China have been indulging in for
years. Read more

brains over ways to make their games sell in Japan, ancient heartland of
mythical beings like Mario, Sonic, and Polaroid Pete. In the late noughties,

targeted console exclusives as Blue Dragon and Lost Odyssey. And Rockstar once

about the abandoned project. Emphasis on the "little" – it doesn't appear to
have gotten very far, despite recently unearthed allusions to "Tokyo PS2" in GTA
5's source code. Read more

items.title: Elections signal cultural shifts that no creative industry can dare to ignore | Opinion
items.description:
There is a perfectly logical way in which you can look at an election result –
even a truly seismic election result – and say that it is largely irrelevant to
the business decision-making of the games industry. Elections do not change your
customer demographics; all of Washington or Westminster or Nagatachō may change
overnight, but the people who bought your games yesterday are still the people
who will buy them tomorrow, aren't they? Read more
items.content:
